newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian forward wool sales tool unveiled.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian forward wool sales tool unveiled.

text.p: Australian wool exporter Prouvost-Hart (Australia) Pty Ltd has introduced a new forward selling scheme at a time when the Australian wool market has produced its most optimistic tone for many months.

The company, a unit of French processor Chargeurs International SA, is introducing a scheme in which woolgrowers will be able to forward sell part of their clip and retain another part for other selling options.
The greatest benefit of the scheme is risk management against market movement, Prouvost-Hart's national manager wool buying Gary Turner said in a statement.
"By forward selling part of their clip, growers are still able to take advantage of the selling options available (and) their year's production is not locked in to one form of disposal," he said.
The wool market was expected to remain volatile, he said.

Prouvost-Hart's new forward selling instrument, which joins Sydney Futures Exchange futures contracts and an over-the-counter forward micron indicator contract being offered by Macquarie Bank, comes as statutory authority Wool International (WI) is strongly promoting risk management and forward marketing as the wool industry's way forward.

This follows collapse of the industry's reserve price scheme six years ago and the build-up of a wool stockpile of almost five million bales in 1991. This has now been reduced to less than two million bales.
Development of the Macquarie Bank scheme has been hindered by a Corporations Law provision which requires users to have assets of more than A$10 million.
Lobbying by Macquarie Bank to have the provision amended had resulted in the opening of talks with the Wool Council of Australia, a spokeswoman for the Australian Securities Commission told Reuters.
"The ASC would be reluctant to talk about it until after the meetings," she said.

The Prouvost-Hart wool buying scheme, however, has been announced after a week of solid wool market gains which took the Eastern Market Indicator 13 cents a kg higher to 621 cents, its highpoint of the season.
Bob Richardson, chief executive officer of Wool International, told Reuters on Friday that the eastern market indicator was expected to average about 600 cents for the whole season to June 30.
For it to do this, the market would need to average about 620 cents for the remainder of the season, he said.
WI expected a gradual improvement in the market, he said.
